vedic_reference.note: The name of the 29th Jain Tirthankara, also mentioned in Hinduism as the name of the Buddha before his enlightenment.

data.cultural_impact: The name Siddharthan holds a significant place in Indian culture, as it was the birth name of Gautama Buddha, the founder of Buddhism. The name evokes images of spiritual enlightenment, success, and fulfillment - ideas that resonate deeply with Hindu and Buddhist philosophies.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Siddharthan represents an individual who has reached the ultimate goal of spiritual growth and self-realization. The name carries the weight of accomplishment and completeness, as the suffix "-an" in Siddharthan suggests that one has attained "ananda," or bliss, in both material and spiritual pursuits. It implies a deep connection to the divine, a sense of inner peace, and an understanding of the true nature of reality.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Siddharthan: One who has attained inner peace and enlightenment, symbolizing a journey from worldly desires to spiritual awakening. The name represents the pursuit of self-realization and the ultimate goal of reaching Nirvana.
